rv.q: Tin Drum Theatre Company's production of The Unseen by Craig Wright is highly recommended.

Steve Needham's sturdy and thoughtful staging (which features an effectively grimy set by Malia Hunter, crepuscular lighting by Jack Goodman, and evocative sound design by Zach Stinnett) provides a quiet and increasingly moving showcase for its three actors—and plenty of unnerving questions for the rest of us.
Those interested can expect an engaging, entertaining experience.
Tin Drum Theatre Company’s production of “The Unseen” should undoubtably be seen—by you!

cn.t: Critics praise this timely, disturbing exploration of torture and authoritarianism as prescient and impactful, though the brutal subject matter makes for heavy viewing. Strong performances elevate Wright's examination of cruelty and complicity.
